messages.content: 一位化學家正在進行一個實驗，使用一個2公斤的特定物質A樣本。實驗開始時，該物質的初始溫度為攝氏25度。然後，化學家將物質加熱到最終溫度攝氏75度。該實驗在1大氣壓力下進行。化學家重複進行相同物質的實驗，但這次的初始溫度為攝氏10度，最終溫度為攝氏50度。你能計算出在這兩個實驗的設定初始和最終條件下，物質的熵變化嗎？

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Entropy Change Formula**

For a material whose heat capacity at constant pressure \(C_{p}\) can be treated as constant over the temperature range considered, the change in entropy when it is heated from an initial temperature \(T_i\) to a final temperature \(T_f\) (both expressed in Kelvin) is

\[
\Delta S \;=\; m\, C_{p}\,\ln\!\left(\frac{T_f}{T_i}\right)
\]

where  
\(m\) – mass of the sample (kg),  
\(C_{p}\) – specific heat capacity at constant pressure (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹).

---

### Assumption about Substance A

The problem statement does **not** specify the identity of “substance A.”  
Because no heat‑capacity data were supplied, we’ll assume that substance A behaves like liquid water, for which

\[
C_{p}^{\text{water}} \;\approx\; 4.184 \times 10^{3}\ \text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}
\]

If you know the actual \(C_{p}\) of your material, simply replace this value in the formulas below.

---

## Experiment 1  
- Mass \(m = 2\ \text{kg}\)  
- Initial temperature \(T_i = 25^\circ\text{C} = 298\ \text{K}\)  
- Final temperature \(T_f = 75^\circ\text{C} = 348\ \text{K}\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta S_1 &= 2\ \text{kg}\; \times\; 4.184\times10^3\ \frac{\text{J}}{\text{kg·K}}\;
            \times\; \ln\!\left(\frac{348}{298}\right) \\[4pt]
          &\approx 2 \times 4.184\times10^3 \times 0.1555 \\[4pt]
          &\approx 1.30 \times 10^3\ \text{J K}^{-1}
\end{aligned}
\]

So, \(\boxed{\Delta S_1 \approx +1.30\ \text{kJ K}^{-1}}\).

---

## Experiment 2  
- Mass \(m = 2\ \text{kg}\)  
- Initial temperature \(T_i = 10^\circ\text{C} = 283\ \text{K}\)  
- Final temperature \(T_f = 50^\circ\text{C} = 323\ \text{K}\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta S_2 &= 2\ \text{kg}\; \times\; 4.184\times10^3\ \frac{\text{J}}{\text{kg·K}}\;
            \times\; \ln\!\left(\frac{323}{283}\right) \\[4pt]
          &\approx 2 \times 4.184\times10^3 \times 0.1325 \\[4pt]
          &\approx 1.11 \times 10^3\ \text{J K}^{-1}
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus, \(\boxed{\Delta S_2 \approx +1.11\ \text{kJ K}^{-1}}\).

---

### Summary Table

| Experiment | \(T_i\) (°C) | \(T_f\) (°C) | \(\Delta S\) (kJ K⁻¹) |
|------------|--------------|--------------|------------------------|
| 1          | 25           | 75           | +1.30                  |
| 2          | 10           | 50           | +1.11                  |

> **Note:**  
> - The positive sign indicates that the entropy of the system increases during heating.  
> - If the real substance has a different \(C_p\), substitute that value into the formula to obtain the correct entropy changes.
